JUDGMENT:

Petitioners filed Claim Petition U/Sec.166 of M.V. Act claiming compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- for the death of deceased Kadri Velu, in road traffic accident occurred on 20.09.2021.
2.

The brief facts of the petition are as under:
On 20.09.2021, at about 9.30 p.m., Kadiri Velu was proceeding on the extreme left side of the road carefully by observing the vehicle movements.

When he was going on 2 nd main road, infront of ICICI Bank ATM, Kasturi Nagar, Bengaluru, at that time the driver of Car bearing Reg.No.KA-04-ML-5818 suddenly came in a rash or negligent manner, endangering to human life without following the traffic rules and dashed against the Kadiri Velu.
Due to the said impact, Kadiri Velu sustained grievous injuries all over the body.

Immediately, Kadiri Velu was shifted to K.R.Puram Government Hospital, after first aid, he was referred to Bowring and Lady Curzon Hospital, Shivajinagar, Bengaluru,
wherein he was succumbed to injuries on 21.09.2021 at about 4.40 a.m., while taking treatment.
After postmortem, dead body was handed over to the petitioners.

The petitioners have shifted the body to their residence and spent Rs.1,00,000/- towards Chinnathayi vs Sridhar.S on 10 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/40132684/
2 funeral and obsequies ceremony.
Due to death of deceased
, the petitioners have suffered mental shock and agony.

The deceased was running cycle shop i.e., selling and servicing and earning Rs.25,000/-
per month.
Due to death of deceased, the petitioners have put to great financial hardship without earning member in the family.
The 1 st petitioner has lost her beloved and care taking husband and petitioner Nos.2 to 6 have lost their love and care taking father.
The accident was occurred due to rash or negligent driving of the driver of Car bearing Reg.No.KA-04-ML-5818.
The K.R. Puram Traffic police have registered a case and filed charge sheet against the driver of aforesaid Car in Cr.No.115/2021 under Sec.279 and 304(A) of IPC.
The 1 st respondent is the R.C. Owner and the 2nd respondent is the insurer of the offending car.
The policy was in force as on the date of accident.
Hence, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.
With these averments they prayed to allow the petition.

3. In response to the notice issued by the Tribunal, the 1st respondent being the R.C. owner of the offending vehicle and the 2nd respondent being the insurer have filed their separate written statements.

4. The written statement averments of 1st respondent is as hereunder:
The 1st respondent denied the entire case of the petitioners and inter-alia contended that, on 20.09.2020 at about 9.20 p.m. he went to xerox shop by driving his Car.
At the time of accident there was a heavy rainfall and the road was under repair due to lay of new big water pipe lane and it was also not good to drive the car more than 30 k.m., speed.
The 1 st respondent was driving the car at the speed of 20 k.m., and he never dashed against the deceased Kadiri Velu.

Further this respondent has denied the date, time and place of accident, rash and negligent driving of the car, injuries sustained by the deceased and his death due to injuries sustained in the accident.
Further denied the occupation and earnings of the deceased.
The deceased was died due to his own negligence as he was drunken and fell himself on the road and not due to alleged accident.
The alleged car not even touched to Kadiri Velu.
The deceased was more than 65 years and he was not in a position to work and earn money.
The compensation claimed by the petitioners is highly excessive and arbitrary.
With these grounds, the 1st respondent prayed to dismiss the petition.

5. The written statement averments of 2 nd respondent is as hereunder:
Respondent No.2 has admitted the issuance of insurance policy with respect to Maruthi Ertiga Car bearing Reg.No.KA-04- ML-5818.

Inter-alia contended that, the Chinnathayi vs Sridhar.S on 10 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/40132684/
3 liability if any is subject to terms and conditions of the policy, valid driving licence held by the driver of offending vehicle.

sentences.text: There is no nexus between the alleged death of deceased and the accident as stated in the petition.
The deceased was stumbled on middle of the road and he was crossed the road in a negligent manner where there was no zebra crossing.
The deceased was the sole responsible for the accident.
After thought, the offending vehicle was introduced to the accident by colluding with the concerned authorities.
The petitioners are not depending on the deceased as the deceased was leaving separately.

Further this respondent has denied the occupation and income of the deceased,
dependency of the petitioners on the deceased.
It is contended that, there is violation of mandatory provision of Sec.134 (c), 158(6) of M.V. Act by the R.C. owner and concerned police.

It is contended that the claim made by the petitioners is excessive,
exorbitant.
With these grounds, the 2nd respondent prayed to dismiss the petition.

6. On the basis of the above pleadings, the predecessor in office has framed the following:
: I S S U E S:
1. Whether petitioners proves that Kadiri Velu was died on 21.09.2021 due to the accident caused by the rash and negligent driving of driver of Car vehicle bearing Registration No.KA-04-ML-5818 on 20.09.2021 as stated in the petition?
2.
Whether the petitioners prove the age and income of the deceased?
3. Whether the respondent No.2 proves alleged contributory negligent on the part of deceased?
4. Whether the petitioners are entitled for the reliefs sought for?
5. What order or award?
7. In order to prove the case of the petitioners, 3 rd petitioner got examined as PW.1 and Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.33 were marked.
P.W.1 was cross-
examined from the side of respondents.
Respondent No.1 got examined as R.W.1.
R.W.1 was cross- examined from the side of petitioners and 2 nd respondent.
2nd respondent has not adduced any evidence.
8. Heard the arguments from both side.
Perused the records placed before the court.

The findings of this Tribunal on the above referred Issues are as hereunder:-
 Issue No.1 :- In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 :- In the Partly Affirmative.
Issue No.3 :- In the Negative.
Issue No.4 :- In the Partly Affirmative.

Issue No.5 :- As per final order for Chinnathayi vs Sridhar.S on 10 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/40132684/
4  the following.

:REASONS:
 9. ISSUE Nos.1 and 3- These two issues are inter connected, hence they were taken together for common discussion in order to avoid repetition.
The petitioners are legal heirs of deceased Kadri Velu.

It is the case of the petitioners that, on 20.09.2021, at about 9.30 p.m., when the deceased Kadri Velu was proceeding as a pedestrian on the extreme left side of the road, he met with the road traffic accident due to rash or negligent driving of the Car bearing Reg.No.KA-04-ML-5818 by its driver and succumbed to the injuries while taking treatment.
To prove their contention, petitioners have lead oral and documentary evidence.
10. The 3rd petitioner, who is the son of deceased Kadiri Velu has examined as P.W.1 and filed affidavit by way of examination in chief and reiterated the averments made in the petition.
Hence this court need not to recapitulate the same once again at this juncture.

In order to prove Issue No.1,
he has produced Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.18.

Ex.P21 is the certified copy of order sheet pertaining to CC No.11474/2022 ( Cr No.115/2021).
11.
According to the respondent Nos.1 and 2, the deceased was stumbled on the middle of the road and crossing the busy road where there was no zebra crossing.
Hence, the deceased himself was sole responsible for the cause of accident.

In order to substantiate the said contentions, respondent No.1 has examined himself as R.W.1 and filed affidavit by way of examination in chief and reiterated the averments made in the written statement.
In support of his evidence, respondent No.1 has not produced any documents.
12. On careful perusal of Ex.P.3, it is crystal clear that, the police have filed charge sheet against Shidhar S.
That apart as per Ex.P1, the accused was arrayed as accused and he was enlarged on bail.
Apart from that 1 st respondent is examined himself as RW.1.
At the time of cross-examination he has admitted that as on the date of accident he went to 2 nd main road, Kasthurinagara.
He also deposed that while issuing reply to the notice issued U/Sec.133 of IMV Act, he has orally informed the police that, he has not caused the accident.
However he has admitted the charge sheet filed against him.
In the instant case the 1st respondent has not produced any documents to show that the accident was not caused on account of his rash or negligence.

At this juncture it is worth to rely on the decision of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka reported in ILR 2003 Karnataka page 493,
Chinnathayi vs Sridhar.S on 10 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/40132684/
5 between Mallamma Vs. Balaji and Others, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka held at para 12 as hereunder:
" Filing of the charge sheet against the driver is also a prima-facie case to hold that,
the driver of the said lorry was responsible for the accident and burden shifts on him to prove the same".
13.

sentences.text: At the cost of repetition, charge sheet has been filed against the 1st respondent.
Therefore, the above referred decision is aptly applicable to the case on hand.

It is manifest that, the materials placed on record by the petitioners are sufficient to believe that, the accident took place due to rash or negligent driving of the driver of the Maruthi Ertiga Car bearing Reg.No.KA- 04-ML-5818.

At the cost of repetition, the contents of complaint and charge sheet clearly reveals that when the deceased was proceeding as a pedestrian on the road, the 1 st respondent/driver of Maruthi Ertiga Car bearing Reg.No.KA-04-ML-5818 drove the vehicle in a rash or negligent manner and dashed against the deceased Kadiri Velu.
The evidence placed on record clearly reveals that 1st respondent/driver of Maruthi Ertiga Car bearing Reg.No.KA-04-ML-5818 has caused the accident.
According to the respondents the deceased Kadiri Velu also contributed for the accident.

In order to prove the same,
there are no materials from the side of respondents.
Hence the contention of respondents regarding the accident was occurred solely on the negligence of deceased Kadiri Velu cannot be accepted.
Accordingly, Issue No.1 is answered in the Affirmative and Issue No.3 is answered in the Negative.
14. ISSUE No.2:-
Age: According to the petitioners, the age of deceased was 62 years at the time of his death.
The petitioners have not produced any documents to show the exact age of the deceased.
As per Ex.P-13- postmortem report of deceased, it reveals that, the deceased was 62 years at the time of his death.
Therefore, this Tribunal is of the opinion that, the aspect of age of deceased need not require elaborate discussion.
Apart from that, there is no serious dispute regarding the age of the deceased.
Hence age of deceased is considered as 62 years at the time of his death.
15. Income of the deceased:- Respondent No.1 and 2 have disputed the income of deceased.

P.W.1 has deposed that his father was running cycle shop i.e., selling, repairing, servicing, puncturing etc.,
and he was earning Rs.25,000/- per month.
However, to substantiate the exact income of the deceased, the petitioners have not produced any documents.
Learned counsel for the respondents vehemently argued that, the son of deceased himself has stated the income of his father as Rs.10,000/- per month.
As such, the same may be considered.
The statement given by the son of deceased cannot be considered as authenticated document.
As such, Ex.P.4 will not come to the aid of respondents to fix the income of deceased.

At this juncture, it is worth to rely on the decision of the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka decided in M.F.A. No.101144 of 2020 ( MV- I) on 05.07.2023,
between Ananda Vs. Arun and Another, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka at Para 9 (b)
as hereunder:
"
In the absence of any cogent material on record, it is for the courts and Tribunals to assess the income notionally.
The notional income fixed by the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority for the accident of the year 2017 is Rs.10,250/-.

Chinnathayi vs Sridhar.S on 10 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/40132684/
6

In the absence of any material produced by the claimant to prove his income, it is appropriate to assess the notional income of the injured claimant at Rs.10,250/- per month, and the same is assessed as the monthly income of the injured claimant".
16.
In the instant case also, the petitioners have not produced the documents to establish the income of deceased.

As such in the absence of reliable document and supportive evidence, the notional income of the deceased is to be considered by relying on the judgment of the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka referred to above.
As per the notional income fixed by the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority for the accident in the year 2021 is Rs.15,000/- per month.
It is pertinent to note that, the accident took place on 20.09.2021.
Hence, the notional income of the deceased is considered as Rs.15,000/- per month.
Accordingly, Issue No.2 is answered in the partly Affirmative.
17. ISSUE No.4:- This issue is with regard to entitlement of relief.
According to the petition averments, petitioner No.1 is the wife, petitioner Nos.2 and 5 are the daughters and petitioner Nos.3, 4 and 6 are the sons of deceased.
The 1 st petitioner has lost her husband and petitioner Nos.2 to 6 have lost their loving father.
Moreover, the bond between the parents and children is an eternal.

At this juncture it is worth to refer the decision of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka rendered in M.F.A.No.102868 of 2014 (M.V.D.), between Reliance General Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs.
Gangappa Saunshi and Others, wherein the Hon'ble High Court held that, "even if the dependency is relevant criteria to claim compensation for loss of dependency, it does not mean financial dependency and the dependency includes gratuitous service dependency, physical dependency,
emotional dependency and psychological dependency so on and so forth, which can never be equated in terms of the money.

entities.text:
Reliance General Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs.
Gangappa Saunshi and Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Even married sons and daughters are entitled for compensation not only on conventional heads, but also on loss of dependency".
Hence, Petitioner Nos.1 to 6 are considered as dependents of deceased.
18. Already this Tribunal has observed that, as on the date of accident the deceased was aged about 62 years.

The Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Pranay Sethi and Others, held that "if the person died in the motor accident, the income with respect to the future prospects has to be taken into consideration while awarding compensation".

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Pranay Sethi and Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It is relevant to note that The Hon'ble Apex Court has provided the chart for the age of the deceased and percentage of future prospects as hereunder:
"If the deceased is self employed or fixed salary, his age below 40 years, future prospects is 40%".
"If the deceased between 40 to 50 years age, future prospects is 25%".
"If the deceased between 50 to 60 years age, future prospects is 10% and if the deceased more than 60 years, no addition as future prospects".
19. Admittedly, the deceased is not a permanent job holder and he is not a fixed salary person.
The deceased was aged about 62 years and therefore, no additional income is added to the income towards future prospects.

So, monthly income of deceased is taken at Rs.15,000/-, which would Chinnathayi vs Sridhar.S on 10 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/40132684/
7 meet the ends of justice.

sentences.text: 20. The 1st petitioner is the wife and other petitioners are the major children of deceased.
Already this Tribunal has observed that, petitioner Nos.1 to 6 are the dependents of the deceased.

Therefore,
by applying the principle laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Sarala Verma case, 1/4th of the income of the deceased has to be deducted towards his personal living expenses.
The same comes to Rs.15,000 - Rs.3,750/- = Rs.11,250/-.
Then total income of the deceased per annum comes to Rs.1,35,000/- (Rs.11,250 x 12 = 1,35,000/-).
21. The deceased was 62 years old at the time of death, the multiplier 7 is applied, which is appropriate to the age of deceased.

Then the loss of dependency is calculated as hereunder:
Rs.1,35,000/- X 7 = Rs.9,45,000/-.
Therefore, this Tribunal deems it just and reasonable to grant compensation of Rs.9,45,000/- under the head of loss of dependency.

22. The Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Co.Ltd., Vs. Pranay Sethi and Others has laid down the guidelines with regard to awarding compensation towards loss of estate, funeral expenses and consortium.

entities.text: National Insurance Co.Ltd., Vs. Pranay Sethi and Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The petitioners have contended that, they have spent Rs.1,00,000/- towards transportation of dead body, funeral and obsequies ceremony expenses of deceased.
In order to substantiate the same, they have not produced any documents.
Now the question before this Tribunal is whether petitioner Nos.1 to 6 are also entitled for consortium or not?
Admittedly, the 1st petitioner is the wife and she is entitled for spousal consortium.
Admittedly the petitioner Nos.2 to 6 are the children of deceased.

At this juncture, it is worth to rely on the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court reported in 2018 (1) SCC 130 between Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Nanuram @
Churu Ram and Others.

entities.text:
Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Nanuram @
Churu Ram and Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Hon'ble Apex Court held that, the parents and children are having right to get the compensation under filial consortium.
Accordingly, the 1 st petitioner is entitled for Rs.44,000/- under the head of spousal consortium and petitioner Nos.2 to 6 are entitled for Rs.44,000/- each under the head of filial consortium.
Further, Rs.16,500/- is awarded for funeral expenses and also Rs.16,500/- is awarded towards loss of estate.

sentences.text: Regarding liability and interest.
24. Driving License:- Charge sheet submitted by IO does not reveals that driver of offending vehicle was driving the vehicle without valid and effective DL.
Hence, it is held that, the driver of offended vehicle was holding valid and effective D.L. as on the date of alleged accident.
25. Insurance Policy:-
In the instant case, respondent No.2 has admitted the issuance of insurance policy with respect to Car bearing Reg.No.KA-04-ML-5818.
Hence, the respondent No.2 shall pay compensation amount to the petitioner.
26. Interest:-

In view of the decision reported in MFA NO: 30131-2019 dtd, 12.5.2020 and M.F.A.No.100090/2014 C/w M.F.A.No.25107/2013 between Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and Others Vs.
Ulrich Belchior Fernandes and Another, rate of interest on the compensation amount is awarded at 6% p.a. from the date of petition.

27. ISSUE No.5:-.

In view of discussion made above, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following:
:ORDER:
Claim Petition filed by the Petitioners U/Sec.166 of M.V. Act is partly allowed with costs of the Petition.
Petitioners are awarded just and reasonable compensation of Rs.12,42,000/-
(Rupees Twelve Lakhs Forty Two Thousand Only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.
from the date of petition to till the date of depositing of the compensation amount in the court.

Respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending vehicle is liable to pay the compensation amount to the petitioners and directed to deposit the compensation amount awarded to the petitioners in the Tribunal within 2 months from the date of this judgment.
Draw award accordingly.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
: APPORTIONMENT OF COMPENSATION :
On deposit of compensation amount, Petitioner No.1 is entitled for 60% and petitioner Nos.2 to 6 are entitled for 8% each with interest.
50% of share of petitioner No.1 with interest is to be paid to her through NEFT/RTGS by way of E-payment on proper identification as per rules and after verifying the stay order from the Hon'ble Appellate Court and remaining 50% of her share with interest Chinnathayi vs Sridhar.S on 10 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/40132684/
9 shall be invested in F.D. in her name in any nationalized bank or scheduled bank of her choice for a period of 3 years.
It is clarified that, the 1 st petitioner is at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on her deposit amount from time to time.
Entire share of petitioner Nos.2 to 6 with interest is to be paid to them through NEFT/RTGS by way of E-payment on proper identification as per rules.

opennyai_summary.facts:
Petitioners filed Claim Petition U/Sec.166 of M.V. Act claiming compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- for the death of deceased Kadri Velu, in road traffic accident occurred on 20.09.2021.
2.
After postmortem, dead body was handed over to the petitioners.
Due to death of deceased, the petitioners have put to great financial hardship without earning member in the family.
The accident was occurred due to rash or negligent driving of the driver of Car bearing Reg.No.KA-04-ML-5818.
The K.R. Puram Traffic police have registered a case and filed charge sheet against the driver of aforesaid Car in Cr.No.115/2021 under Sec.279 and 304(A) of IPC.
The 1 st respondent is the R.C. Owner and the 2nd respondent is the insurer of the offending car.
The policy was in force as on the date of accident.
Hence, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.
The deceased was died due to his own negligence as he was drunken and fell himself on the road and not due to alleged accident.
The compensation claimed by the petitioners is highly excessive and arbitrary.
There is no nexus between the alleged death of deceased and the accident as stated in the petition.
The deceased was the sole responsible for the accident.
It is contended that, there is violation of mandatory provision of Sec.134 (c), 158(6) of M.V. Act by the R.C. owner and concerned police.
opennyai_summary.issue:
6. On the basis of the above pleadings, the predecessor in office has framed the following:
: I S S U E S:
1. Whether petitioners proves that Kadiri Velu was died on 21.09.2021 due to the accident caused by the rash and negligent driving of driver of Car vehicle bearing Registration No.KA-04-ML-5818 on 20.09.2021 as stated in the petition?
2.
Whether the petitioners prove the age and income of the deceased?
3. Whether the respondent No.2 proves alleged contributory negligent on the part of deceased?
4. Whether the petitioners are entitled for the reliefs sought for?
5. What order or award?
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
In the instant case the 1st respondent has not produced any documents to show that the accident was not caused on account of his rash or negligence.
It is manifest that, the materials placed on record by the petitioners are sufficient to believe that, the accident took place due to rash or negligent driving of the driver of the Maruthi Ertiga Car bearing Reg.No.KA- 04-ML-5818.
At the cost of repetition, the contents of complaint and charge sheet clearly reveals that when the deceased was proceeding as a pedestrian on the road, the 1 st respondent/driver of Maruthi Ertiga Car bearing Reg.No.KA-04-ML-5818 drove the vehicle in a rash or negligent manner and dashed against the deceased Kadiri Velu.
The evidence placed on record clearly reveals that 1st respondent/driver of Maruthi Ertiga Car bearing Reg.No.KA-04-ML-5818 has caused the accident.
The petitioners have not produced any documents to show the exact age of the deceased.
As per Ex.P-13- postmortem report of deceased, it reveals that, the deceased was 62 years at the time of his death.
Therefore, this Tribunal is of the opinion that, the aspect of age of deceased need not require elaborate discussion.
Apart from that, there is no serious dispute regarding the age of the deceased.
Hence age of deceased is considered as 62 years at the time of his death.
In the instant case also, the petitioners have not produced the documents to establish the income of deceased.
As such in the absence of reliable document and supportive evidence, the notional income of the deceased is to be considered by relying on the judgment of the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka referred to above.
At this juncture it is worth to refer the decision of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka rendered in M.F.A.No.102868 of 2014 (M.V.D.), between Reliance General Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs.
Gangappa Saunshi and Others, wherein the Hon'ble High Court held that, "even if the dependency is relevant criteria to claim compensation for loss of dependency, it does not mean financial dependency and the dependency includes gratuitous service dependency, physical dependency,
emotional dependency and psychological dependency so on and so forth, which can never be equated in terms of the money.
Hence, Petitioner Nos.1 to 6 are considered as dependents of deceased.
19. Admittedly, the deceased is not a permanent job holder and he is not a fixed salary person.
The deceased was aged about 62 years and therefore, no additional income is added to the income towards future prospects.
So, monthly income of deceased is taken at Rs.15,000/-, which would Chinnathayi vs Sridhar.S on 10 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/40132684/
7 meet the ends of justice.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Admittedly the petitioner Nos.2 to 6 are the children of deceased.
The Hon'ble Apex Court held that, the parents and children are having right to get the compensation under filial consortium.
Accordingly, the 1 st petitioner is entitled for Rs.44,000/- under the head of spousal consortium and petitioner Nos.2 to 6 are entitled for Rs.44,000/- each under the head of filial consortium.
Further, Rs.16,500/- is awarded for funeral expenses and also Rs.16,500/- is awarded towards loss of estate.
23. The details of compensation amount is as under:
 S.No. Heads Rs.
 1. Towards loss of Rs. 9,45,000/-
 Dependency.
2 . Towards spousal and Rs. 2,64,000/-
 filial consortium, 44,000 X 6
3. Loss of Estate Rs. 16,500/-
 4. Funeral expense Rs. 16,500/-
Total Rs
Hence, petitioners are entitled for just and reasonable amount of Rs.12,42,000/-
Chinnathayi vs Sridhar.S on 10 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/40132684/
8
Hence, it is held that, the driver of offended vehicle was holding valid and effective D.L. as on the date of alleged accident.
In the instant case, respondent No.2 has admitted the issuance of insurance policy with respect to Car bearing Reg.No.KA-04-ML-5818.
Hence, the respondent No.2 shall pay compensation amount to the petitioner.
In view of the decision reported in MFA NO: 30131-2019 dtd, 12.5.2020 and M.F.A.No.100090/2014 C/w M.F.A.No.25107/2013 between Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and Others Vs.
Ulrich Belchior Fernandes and Another, rate of interest on the compensation amount is awarded at 6% p.a. from the date of petition.
Accordingly, Issue No.4 is answered in the Partly Affirmative.
In view of discussion made above, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following:
:ORDER:
Claim Petition filed by the Petitioners U/Sec.166 of M.V. Act is partly allowed with costs of the Petition.
Petitioners are awarded just and reasonable compensation of Rs.12,42,000/-
(Rupees Twelve Lakhs Forty Two Thousand Only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.
from the date of petition to till the date of depositing of the compensation amount in the court.
Respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending vehicle is liable to pay the compensation amount to the petitioners and directed to deposit the compensation amount awarded to the petitioners in the Tribunal within 2 months from the date of this judgment.
Draw award accordingly.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
: APPORTIONMENT OF COMPENSATION :
On deposit of compensation amount, Petitioner No.1 is entitled for 60% and petitioner Nos.2 to 6 are entitled for 8% each with interest.
50% of share of petitioner No.1 with interest is to be paid to her through NEFT/RTGS by way of E-payment on proper identification as per rules and after verifying the stay order from the Hon'ble Appellate Court and remaining 50% of her share with interest Chinnathayi vs Sridhar.S on 10 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/40132684/
9 shall be invested in F.D. in her name in any nationalized bank or scheduled bank of her choice for a period of 3 years.
It is clarified that, the 1 st petitioner is at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on her deposit amount from time to time.
Entire share of petitioner Nos.2 to 6 with interest is to be paid to them through NEFT/RTGS by way of E-payment on proper identification as per rules.
